handbookNote: Indiana Driver's Manual, Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles (in.gov/bmv/licenses-permits-ids/files/drivers-manual.pdf) -- current edition, internally dated July 2026 (per its own closing page: 'Published July 2026 | Check IN.gov/BMV for updates'), fetched directly from the official BMV website on 2026-08-16 and extracted with pdftotext (full text saved to temp/handbooks/in/driver.txt, 4,446 lines / ~289KB). Real exam mechanics were researched from three official BMV sources that all agree: the manual itself (Chapter 1, Knowledge Exam; Chapter 9, Knowledge Exam Sample Questions), the BMV's dedicated Knowledge Exam webpage (in.gov/bmv/.../learners-permit/knowledge-exam), and the BMV's official Practice Knowledge Exam PDF. All three CONFIRM: the standard learner's permit/driver's license knowledge exam is a computer-based, multiple-choice exam with two components -- a sign-recognition component and a traffic-rules/laws component -- and you must score 80% or higher correct on EACH component to pass. The BMV does NOT publish an official total item count or a time limit for this base exam anywhere in the manual or on its website (this is confirmed absent, not guessed), so those two figures are left explicitly unconfirmed rather than invented. For contrast/context only (not used as the base exam's numbers): the manual's separate For-Hire and Motor Driven Cycle endorsement exams are each explicitly stated to be 25 questions with a maximum of 5 misses (80%) to pass. This is an unusually rich, detailed 75-page manual covering credentialing and the knowledge/skills exam process, restrictions and endorsements (including motorcycle, MDC, autocycle, for-hire), watercraft/organ donation/parking placards, renewing/amending/replacing credentials, points/suspensions/insurance/Habitual Traffic Violator rules, a full traffic signs and signals chapter, an extensive safe-vehicle-operation chapter (lane markings, turning, speed limits, following distance, skidding/rollover, weather and night driving, distracted/drowsy/aggressive driving, work zones, railroad crossings, sharing the road with trucks/motorcycles/bicycles/pedestrians/school buses, parking, seat belts/child restraints, truck equipment), and a full accidents/emergencies chapter -- comfortably supporting a large, non-repetitive, well-grounded question bank at this project's standard Driver track price ($4.99). Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official manual text (or, for the small number of exam-mechanics questions, the corroborating official BMV webpage/PDF); none are invented, generic 'common knowledge,' or copied verbatim from the manual's own sample-question set.
